key_insight: LLM-agent probability reports can violate complement consistency: a claim and its opposite do not reliably receive probabilities that sum to one.
engineering_relevance: Validate consistency under complementary wording before interpreting simulated agent probabilities as beliefs or using them in iterative network simulations.
method: Pair each claim with its complement, replacing prior and neighbor probabilities p with 1 − p.
Evaluate Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Gemma-3-4B using simulation states, fact-checking claims, and controlled two-outcome worlds.
Track complementary populations over repeated rounds and test a paired-answer averaging correction.
evidence_signal: Across 2,304 simulation states, Qwen’s paired reports averaged 1.18 in total; controlled tests found failures in all three models, with discrepancies 2–10 times larger than same-meaning paraphrase effects.
watch_item: Paired-answer averaging enforces consistency and lowers Brier loss averaged across wordings, but beats the better original wording at the final round for only one of three models.
paper_title: Do "True" and "False" Add Up to One? Complement Consistency in LLM-Agent Opinion Simulations
